recent.text: Owned a real feature end to end, from design doc to production rollout.
Real flight-hardware exposure and engineers who explain the why behind decisions.
Clean dataset access, a patient manager, and a final project the client actually used.
Small team, so I got to test code on physical robots in my second week.
Friendly staff and a clear look at how a community bank runs day to day.

meridianReviews.pros: Owned a real feature end to end, from design doc to production rollout. My mentor reviewed every pull request within a day and the team treated interns like teammates, not coffee runners.
meridianReviews.cons: Onboarding was a firehose in the first two weeks and the internal tooling has a steep learning curve. Parking downtown is not covered.
meridianReviews.day: Standup at 9:30, heads-down on my feature until lunch, code review and pairing in the afternoon. Fridays were demo day with the whole org.

meridianReviews.pros: Strong mentorship, well-scoped project, and the pay is hard to beat. I shipped a latency fix that actually moved a dashboard metric.
meridianReviews.cons: Remote interns miss out on some of the in-person networking. Time zones made a couple of syncs awkward.
meridianReviews.day: Async updates in Slack, two scheduled pairing sessions a day, and a short written summary at end of day.

meridianReviews.pros: Got hands-on with Terraform and Kubernetes on real internal services, with a mentor who walked through every change.
meridianReviews.cons: The interview loop was long, and on-call shadowing started before I felt ready.
meridianReviews.day: Morning standup, infrastructure tickets until lunch, then pairing with an SRE on deployments.

meridianReviews.pros: Built a data-quality check that now runs on every nightly load, and the team let me present it at the all-hands.
meridianReviews.cons: A lot of time went to waiting on access requests in the first week.
meridianReviews.day: Query reviews in the morning, pipeline work after lunch, and a weekly one-on-one with my manager.
